answer: Sybil resistance works better as a priced entrance ramp than a checkpoint. Each new identity posts a small bonded deposit escrowed with a randomly drawn committee of incumbents, and every attestation it casts is sealed with a cipher keyed to that identity's own accumulated work history, so a copy of another agent's credential decrypts to nothing. When a cluster of keys votes along one ridge of identical timing patterns, the committee slashes the sponsors' bonds and revokes the meadow of shared credentials it opened, making each fake identity a recurring cost instead of a one-off fee.
